getLawyer.why: If you are arrested or detained in Portugal, ask for a lawyer and for the Canadian consular office to be notified (Embassy of Canada (Lisbon): +351 21 316 4600). Sign nothing you do not understand. Dual citizenship is recognized, but Canadian consular help may be limited.

Penalties for possession, use or trafficking of illegal drugs in Portugal are severe — jail or heavy fines. Contact the Canadian consular office and get a local lawyer; say and sign nothing without counsel.

deadlines.title: Schengen 90/180 — max 90 days in any 180
deadlines.rule: Canadians need no visa for up to 90 DAYS in any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen area. Your passport must be valid at least 3 MONTHS beyond the date you expect to leave the Schengen area. The Entry/Exit System (EES) records biometric data on arrival; ETIAS will be required once it opens — apply only on the official EU website. Dual citizens of a participating country must travel on their European passport.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Portugal

deadlines.title: Drive up to 185 days on a Canadian licence (0.05% alcohol limit)
deadlines.rule: A valid Canadian licence can be used for up to 185 DAYS if you are not a Portuguese resident. Minimum driving age 18. Blood-alcohol limit 0.05%. Keep a reflective vest and warning triangle in the vehicle (triangle placed at least 30 metres behind the car); low-beam headlights at all times; child seats for children under 12 or under 135 cm.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Portugal

statutes.title: Identification
statutes.summary: Carry valid photo ID at all times — local authorities can ask to see it. Carry a photocopy or digital copy of your passport and keep another copy somewhere safe.

book.title: Police, ID, and if you're detained in Portugal
book.overview: Carry valid photo ID at all times — local authorities can ask to see it. Carry a photocopy or digital copy of your passport and keep another copy somewhere safe. If you are arrested or detained, ask for a lawyer and ask that the Canadian consular office be told. Emergency: 112. Dual citizenship is recognized, but Canadian consular help may be limited.
your_rights: Ask for a lawyer before answering questions.
Ask the authorities to notify the Canadian consular office.
Ask for an interpreter if you do not understand the language.
Do not sign anything you do not understand.
key_steps: Carry ID (or a copy) as the local rules require.
If detained: ask for a lawyer, an interpreter, and the Canadian consular office.
Save the emergency number (112) and the consular contact (+351 21 316 4600).
Report theft to the police to get a report for insurance.
common_mistakes: Not carrying ID or a copy.
Assuming dual citizenship guarantees Canadian consular help.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately on arrest or detention — ask for a lawyer and the Canadian consular office.

your_rights: Entry without a visa for the tourist period stated, if you meet the passport-validity rule.
To be told the reason if you are refused entry.
To contact the Canadian consular office if you are detained at the border.

Count your days carefully and keep proof of your entry date.

book.title: Local laws that catch visitors in Portugal
book.overview: Penalties for possession, use or trafficking of illegal drugs are severe — convicted offenders can expect jail sentences or heavy fines. Other local rules that surprise visitors: Photographing police, military, or sensitive installations is prohibited. Filming or photographing people without their consent is illegal. Causing a forest fire is a criminal offence, even if accidental. Drug penalties can include fines, administrative sanctions, mandatory treatment, or jail — do not carry packages for others.
your_rights: The right to a lawyer if you are charged.
The right to have the Canadian consular office notified.
The right to an interpreter in proceedings you do not understand.
key_steps: Do not carry packages or luggage for anyone else.
Learn the local rules below before you go — ignorance is not a defence.
Photographing police, military, or sensitive installations is prohibited.
Filming or photographing people without their consent is illegal.
common_mistakes: Assuming rules are the same as in Canada.
Carrying or using drugs because they seem tolerated locally.
book.when_lawyer: As soon as you are questioned about, or charged with, any offence.

book.title: Crime, scams and driving in Portugal
book.overview: Pickpocketing and bag snatching are common in busy tourist areas and on trams, especially in Lisbon and Porto; drink spiking is a risk in bars and nightclubs. Driving: A valid Canadian licence can be used for up to 185 DAYS if you are not a Portuguese resident. Minimum driving age 18. Blood-alcohol limit 0.05%. Keep a reflective vest and warning triangle in the vehicle (triangle placed at least 30 metres behind the car); low-beam headlights at all times; child seats for children under 12 or under 135 cm.
your_rights: To report a crime to the police and receive a report for insurance.
To consular assistance from Canada if you are a victim of crime.
To drive on your Canadian licence for the period stated, if you meet the conditions.
key_steps: Keep valuables out of sight and bags closed in crowds and on transit.
Use only licensed taxis and check ATMs before using your card.
Carry the required safety equipment and documents when driving.
Report theft promptly and contact your card issuer.
common_mistakes: Leaving valuables in a parked car.
Driving without the required permit, equipment, or insurance.
Ignoring local traffic-zone and alcohol rules.
book.when_lawyer: After a serious collision, any arrest, or a significant theft or fraud.
